reviewers.summary: The passcode flow reveals the seeded-user list without validating the passcode, and sign-in omits the required anti-forgery header. The tests also do not catch the premature picker behavior.

findingList.message: The seeded-user picker is shown before the passcode is validated, contrary to the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: continueWithPasscode checks only that passcode is nonempty, then fetches /api/auth/users without sending or validating it and displays the response.
evidence.failureScenario: A visitor enters an incorrect nonempty passcode and /api/auth/users returns the seeded users; the picker appears before the passcode is validated, exposing the roster (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

findingList.message: The sign-in request omits the required anti-forgery header, despite the criterion requiring it on every state-changing request.

evidence.codePathTraced: signIn sends a state-changing POST to /api/auth/sign-in with only a Content-Type header; it does not send the required anti-forgery token.
evidence.failureScenario: When the server requires the specified anti-forgery header, submitting sign-in omits it and the request is rejected (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

findingList.message: The tests do not cover the first criterion's requirement that users appear only after a successful passcode step.

evidence.codePathTraced: The passcode-step test checks that users appear after entering a nonempty value. The wrong-passcode test checks the generic message only after the picker appears and sign-in is submitted.
evidence.failureScenario: If any nonempty passcode reveals the picker, these tests still pass; they do not verify that an incorrect passcode keeps the picker hidden as required by the first acceptance criterion.

reviewers.summary: The change exposes the seeded-user picker before passcode validation and omits the required anti-forgery header on sign-in. The tests also do not catch the missing passcode gate.

findingList.message: The seeded-user picker is shown without validating the passcode, contrary to the first acceptance criterion. This exposes user metadata before the sign-in gate (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

evidence.codePathTraced: continueWithPasscode checks only that the field is nonempty, then fetches /api/auth/users and displays the response without sending or validating the passcode.
evidence.failureScenario: A visitor enters an incorrect nonempty passcode and /api/auth/users returns the seeded users; the picker appears before the passcode has been accepted.

findingList.message: The sign-in request omits the required anti-forgery header, despite the second acceptance criterion requiring it on every state-changing request (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

evidence.codePathTraced: signIn sends a state-changing POST to /api/auth/sign-in with only a Content-Type header; it does not send the required anti-forgery token.
evidence.failureScenario: When the server requires the specified anti-forgery header, submitting the sign-in form omits it and the server rejects the request.

findingList.message: The tests do not verify that an incorrect passcode keeps the seeded-user picker hidden, as required by the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: The test enters a valid-looking nonempty passcode and checks that the picker appears; no test enters an incorrect passcode and checks that the picker stays hidden.
evidence.failureScenario: If any nonempty passcode reveals the picker, the current test still passes, so the first acceptance criterion's passcode gate is not tested.

reviewers.summary: The passcode step reveals the seeded-user picker without validating the passcode, and the sign-in POST omits the required anti-forgery header. The tests check the token only on sign-out.

findingList.message: The seeded-user picker is exposed before the passcode is validated, contrary to the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: continueWithPasscode checks only that the field is nonempty, then fetches /api/auth/users without sending or validating the passcode and displays the response.
evidence.failureScenario: An unauthenticated visitor enters any nonempty value; if /api/auth/users returns the seeded users, their names and roles are shown without a successful passcode step (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

findingList.message: The sign-in request omits the required anti-forgery token header.

evidence.codePathTraced: The state-changing POST to /api/auth/sign-in sends only Content-Type and does not include the required anti-forgery token header.
evidence.failureScenario: When the server requires the specified anti-forgery header, submitting the sign-in form omits it and the request is rejected (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

findingList.message: The tests do not verify the anti-forgery header on sign-in, as required by the second acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: The anti-forgery assertion checks only the sign-out request; no test checks the sign-in request header, despite the acceptance criterion requiring the header on every state-changing request.
evidence.failureScenario: If the sign-in POST omits its required token, the named test file still passes, so the acceptance criterion requiring the header is not verified.
